title: hardware-comparison-benchmarks-a100-h100-l40s-drivers-cuda
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the end-to-end benchmarks and profiling runs comparing NVIDIA A100, H100, and L40S GPUs across a set of cloud SKUs and driver / CUDA permutations. The goal was to identify performance regressions and best-practice driver/CUDA pairings for our serving runtime (v2.3.1) under realistic inference workloads: short-chat (512 tokens), long-context generation (8k tokens), and batched embeddings.

High-level takeaway:
- H100 gives the best raw throughput for large-context workloads (8k) at CUDA 12.x, but is sensitive to driver/CUDA mismatch — observed kernel timeouts when mixing older drivers with CUDA 12.
- A100 remains the most cost-stable option with predictable latency and works well on CUDA 11.8 with driver 520.x for our FP16 and quantized kernels.
- L40S shows strong single-stream latency (p50) and is an attractive option for latency-sensitive, smaller models; memory layout differences require small inference-engine workarounds (see notes).
- Recommendation: For Hosted API default tier keep A100 (CUDA 11.8 / driver 520) as baseline; Dedicated high-perf tier use H100 (CUDA 12.1+ / driver 535+) for long-context models and customers who need max throughput.

Environment and SKUs tested:
- AWS p4d.24xlarge (8x A100 40GB) — CUDA 11.8 / NVIDIA driver 520.56.06; CUDA 12.x tests with driver 525 were attempted but showed no perf win for our kernels.
- AWS p5.48xlarge (8x H100 80GB) — CUDA 12.1 / NVIDIA driver 535.54.03; also tested CUDA 12.2 with driver 540 for kernel stability.
- GCP a2-megagpu-16g (16x A100 40GB) — CUDA 11.8 / driver 520.61.05 (GCP package).
- GCP h100-8 (8x H100 80GB) — CUDA 12.1 / driver 535.65.01.
- Azure NVv4/L40s-skus (L40S 48GB) — CUDA 12.2 / driver 540.86.01 (verified on the preview SKU).

Software stack:
- Serving runtime: internal v2.3.1 (compiled with cuBLAS/cuDNN dynamic linking), build flags: -O3 -march=native, tensor core FP16 enabled, optimized kernel selection on.
- Models: opt-6.7b-m2 (quantized 4-bit), llama-13b (FP16), embeddings: text-embed-3-small (FP16).
- Workloads: single-stream autoregressive generation, batch size sweep (1,2,4,8), seq-len sweep (512,2048,8192), embeddings batches (1,8,32).
- Measurement harness: 30-minute runs for each cell, steady-state window used for metrics (discard first 5 minutes). Metrics captured: tokens/s (throughput), p50/p95 latency (ms), GPU memory utilization, CPU utilization, kernel error counts.

Experiment matrix (representative cells):
- A100: CUDA 11.8 / driver 520 (AWS p4d), CUDA 12.1 / driver 525 (GCP attempt)
- H100: CUDA 12.1 / driver 535, CUDA 12.2 / driver 540
- L40S: CUDA 12.2 / driver 540 (Azure preview)

Representative results (steady-state):
1) Long-context generation (llama-13b FP16, seq=8192, batch=1, temperature=0.0, greedy)
- AWS p5 (H100, CUDA12.1): throughput 18.5 tokens/s, p50 latency per token 54 ms, p95 82 ms, GPU mem 60GB used, observed stable with driver 535.
- GCP h100-8 (H100, CUDA12.1): throughput 17.9 tokens/s, p50 56 ms, p95 88 ms — minor variance likely due to networking and instance sizing.
- AWS p4d (A100, CUDA11.8): throughput 10.8 tokens/s, p50 92 ms, p95 140 ms, GPU mem 38GB used.
- Azure L40S (CUDA12.2): throughput 12.4 tokens/s, p50 78 ms, p95 120 ms, but single-token latency jitter lower than A100.

2) Short-chat generation (opt-6.7b quant-4, seq=512, batch=8)
- A100 (CUDA11.8): throughput 1,200 tokens/s aggregate, p50 latency 18 ms, p95 35 ms.
- H100 (CUDA12.1): throughput 1,550 tokens/s, p50 14 ms, p95 28 ms.
- L40S (CUDA12.2): throughput 1,320 tokens/s, p50 16 ms, p95 32 ms.

3) Embeddings (text-embed-3-small, batch 32)
- A100: 6,400 emb/s, GPU mem 20GB; CPU offload negligible.
- H100: 8,200 emb/s, GPU mem 24GB; best when using CUDA12.1+ and cuBLASLt fused kernels.
- L40S: 7,100 emb/s, GPU mem 22GB.

Profiling notes and bottlenecks observed:
- Kernel selection and GEMM tiling differences (cuBLAS/cuBLASLt) account for most of the H100 win on long-context models; our runtime was not automatically selecting the newer cuBLASLt kernels on some driver combos — explicit kernel hints in runtime recovered most of the gap.
- KV-cache memcpy hotspots: on A100 we observed higher PCIe host-device memcpy overhead when using smaller batches; NVLink-connected instances (p4d/p5) reduce this but differences remain across cloud vendors.
- Attention kernel degradation: H100 shows improved attention performance when running with CUDA 12.1+ and driver 535+, likely due to optimized attention kernels. When using CUDA 11.x on H100 emulation layers, attention kernels fell back and performance dropped ~30%.
- L40S memory layout: the card exposes different optimal alignment for our custom quantized kernels — small change in block size (to 128 vs 256) improved throughput by ~7%.
- Driver mismatches: several runs with CUDA 12.2 + 520-driver combinations caused increased kernel launch failures and occasional OOM reports under stress. Keep driver and CUDA minor versions aligned with vendor recommendations.

Recommendations / Action items:
- Standardize baseline host images: A100 baseline image: CUDA 11.8 + driver 520.x (certified); H100 baseline image: CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.x. Add image variants for CUDA 12.2 where L40S is primary. (Owner: Infra, due: 2025-12-15)
- Runtime changes: expose explicit cuBLASLt kernel hints for H100 and fallback ordering for A100 to avoid suboptimal kernel picks (Owner: serving-runtime, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482).
- Add L40S alignment config flag in quantized kernel path and include auto-tuning step at first-run to detect optimal block size (Owner: applied-ml).
- Testing matrix: extend CI performance jobs to include one H100 and one L40S SKU with CUDA 12.1/12.2 for regressions. (Owner: release-engineering)
- Public guidance: update docs/console to recommend GPU + driver combos for customers (Hosted default vs Dedicated suggestions).

Known issues and follow-ups:
- Reproduce kernel timeouts seen occasionally on H100 when using older drivers — root cause suspected to be driver scheduler interactions under high host-side thread pressure. (Investigating with vendor support)
- Quantization fallback: some quantized kernels produce lower throughput on A100 when using cuBLASLt fallback path; need to measure accuracy cost if switching to different tiling options.

Raw data and artifacts:
- Raw CSVs and flamegraphs uploaded to: s3://redwood-bench/hw-comparison/2025-11-20/ (internal access only).
- Perf harness commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/commit/9f3b7c2

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing a cell
1. Provision instance (note exact SKU) and ensure NVLINK / NCCL topology matches the p4d/p5 reference.
2. Use baseline image (A100: CUDA11.8+driver520, H100: CUDA12.1+driver535).
3. Pull serving-runtime:v2.3.1 and perf-harness commit above.
4. Warmup: run 5 minutes of synthetic requests.
5. Run 30-minute measured job; collect p50/p95, tokens/s, GPU mem, and kernel errors.

If you need a condensed slide or a spreadsheet of the full matrix for exec review I can produce it — flagged for Alex to assemble the slide deck.

Signed,
Priya Patel
Senior SRE (serving-runtime)
